html:
Choctaw (Oklahoma) marks the land of the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma, in the southeast corner of the state, with its headquarters at Durant. The Choctaw came from Mississippi and Alabama; see Chahta Yakni for their homeland.

Under the Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek in 1830 they gave up their land in Mississippi, and from 1831 they were the first of the southeastern nations sent west on the Trail of Tears. Thousands died on the way. In Indian Territory they set up a government with a constitution, schools and courts. In 1847, while still poor themselves, they sent a gift of money to Ireland during the Great Famine, which Ireland still remembers. In the First World War Choctaw soldiers used their language to send messages the Germans could not read. Their land was allotted before Oklahoma became a state in 1907.
